summary: Zolbetuximab (Vyloy) is a CLDN18.2-directed cytolytic antibody indicated with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy for first-line treatment of adults with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-negative gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma whose tumors are CLDN18.2 positive by an FDA-approved test, based on the SPOTLIGHT and GLOW trials. The recommended first dose is 800 mg/m2 IV followed by 600 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or 400 mg/m2 every 2 weeks. It is emetogenic: premedicate with antiemetics before each infusion. Serious and fatal hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis and infusion-related reactions have occurred; monitor during and for at least 2 hours after infusion. There are no absolute contraindications in labeling.
indications: First-line treatment of adults with locally advanced unresectable or metastatic HER2-negative gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma whose tumors are CLDN18.2 positive, in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy

dosage.d: 800 mg/m2 IV as the first dose
dosage.t: Single first infusion at the initial rate for 30-60 min, then the subsequent rate as tolerated
dosage.n: Give only by IV infusion, never push or bolus; confirm CLDN18.2 positivity before starting

dosage.t: Every 3 weeks with chemotherapy until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: No dose reduction recommended; manage reactions by rate reduction, interruption, withholding, or discontinuation

dosage.t: Every 2 weeks with chemotherapy until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Same reaction management; see admin for infusion rates

dosage.d: No dose reduction; interrupt, slow, withhold, or permanently discontinue by severity
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue for severe or life-threatening hypersensitivity or IRR

admin: Administer only by IV infusion; do not give as IV push or bolus
Premedicate before each infusion with a combination of antiemetics (e.g., NK-1 and/or 5-HT3 blockers, plus other agents as indicated)
Start each infusion at the initial rate for 30-60 min; if no reaction, increase to the subsequent rate as tolerated (first dose 800 mg/m2: 100 mg/m2/h then 200-265 mg/m2/h per labeling)

Monitor during infusion and for at least 2 hours after completion (longer if indicated) for hypersensitivity (urticaria, wheeze, throat tightness, voice change) and IRR signs (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, chills, pyrexia, chest discomfort, hypertension)
For Grade 2 hypersensitivity or IRR, interrupt until Grade <=1 then resume at reduced rate; premedicate subsequent infusions with antihistamines
Use diluted bag within 6 hours at room temperature or 16 hours refrigerated (2-8 C) from end of preparation to end of infusion; discard and prepare a new bag if time is exceeded
moa: Zolbetuximab-clzb is a CLDN18.2-directed cytolytic antibody that binds claudin 18.2 on tumor cells and depletes them via antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC). Combined with chemotherapy it showed increased antitumor activity in CLDN18.2-expressing mouse tumor models compared with either alone.

relative: History of severe hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis to zolbetuximab
Pregnancy (use only if benefit outweighs risk; chemotherapy partners carry their own fetal risk)
Active significant vomiting or dehydration risk (emetogenic therapy)
monitor: Signs of hypersensitivity or IRR during and >=2 h after each infusion
Nausea/vomiting severity, hydration status, and electrolytes

preg: There are no data with zolbetuximab use in pregnant women. In mice given IV zolbetuximab during organogenesis, no embryo-fetal toxicity occurred at up to 300 mg/kg (about 1.9 times the clinical dose by AUC); the antibody crossed the placenta with higher fetal than maternal serum levels. Give to a pregnant woman only if benefit outweighs potential risk. Refer to the fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy labels for pregnancy testing, contraception, and infertility information.
lact: There are no data on zolbetuximab in human milk, its effects on the breastfed child, or milk production. Because antibodies may be excreted in milk and serious reactions are possible, advise a lactating woman not to breastfeed during treatment and for 8 months after the last dose.
renal: Mild to moderate renal impairment (CLcr 30 to <90 mL/min) had no clinically important effect on clearance. The effect of severe renal impairment is unknown; no dose recommendation is established. Maintain hydration given vomiting risk.
hepatic: Mild hepatic impairment (TB <=ULN with AST >ULN, or TB >1 to 1.5 x ULN with any AST) had no clinically important effect on clearance. The effect of moderate to severe hepatic impairment is unknown.

major: Other highly emetogenic chemotherapy - additive nausea/vomiting; coordinate scheduled antiemetics
moderate: Agents requiring rate-sensitive infusion monitoring - additive IRR management burden during co-infusion days
minor: No formal drug interaction studies described; monoclonal antibody with target-mediated disposition, CYP-mediated interactions not expected
interactions.food: Not applicable (IV); maintain hydration and antiemetic schedule around infusions
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; avoid excess alcohol during chemotherapy
interactions.diagnostics: Common lab abnormalities include decreased neutrophils, leukocytes, albumin, hemoglobin, lymphocytes, platelets, glucose, sodium, phosphate, potassium, magnesium; increased creatinine, glucose, AST, alkaline phosphatase, ALT

serious: Serious hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis (severe in 2%)
Severe nausea and vomiting leading to dehydration
Serious neutropenia and febrile neutropenia (with chemotherapy)
Intestinal obstruction, sepsis, pneumonia, respiratory failure (serious events in trials, some fatal)
rare: Fatal infusion-related reactions (0.4% discontinued for IRR)
Acute hepatic failure and fatal sepsis/pneumonia in combination trials
emergency: Anaphylaxis (hives, wheeze, throat tightness, voice change, hypotension) - stop infusion and treat immediately
Intractable vomiting with dehydration or inability to keep fluids down
Fever with neutropenia, severe abdominal pain, or breathing difficulty

monitoring: CLDN18.2 positivity by an FDA-approved test before starting
Vitals and hypersensitivity/IRR symptoms during infusion and for >=2 h after
Nausea/vomiting control, oral intake, hydration, body weight, electrolytes
CBC and renal function with chemotherapy cycles
counsel: This drug is given by vein with chemotherapy, usually every 2 or 3 weeks; report any prior severe infusion or allergy reaction
Nausea and vomiting are very common, worst in the first cycle; take anti-nausea medicines as directed and call if you cannot keep fluids down
Nurses will watch you during and for at least 2 hours after the drip; report hives, itching, cough, wheeze, throat tightness, chills, fever, or chest discomfort at once
Tell your team about fever, severe belly pain, swelling, black stools, or signs of infection
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 8 months after the last dose; discuss pregnancy plans because chemotherapy partners can harm a fetus
pk: Antitumor effect accrues over cycles with chemotherapy; infusion exposure is immediate
Geometric mean Cmax about 415 mcg/mL at steady state (800 mg/m2 first dose then 600 mg/m2 q3w)
Geometric mean about 41 days; clearance about 0.013 L/h
Steady state by about 18 weeks; dosed every 2 or 3 weeks with chemotherapy; long half-life sustains exposure between cycles
Vials refrigerated 2-8 C (36-46 F) in original carton; do not freeze or shake; diluted bag: room temperature <=6 h or refrigerated 2-8 C <=16 h from preparation to end of infusion
pearls: First CLDN18.2-directed therapy for HER2-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; requires FDA-approved CLDN18.2 testing (SPOTLIGHT with mFOLFOX6, GLOW with CAPOX)
No dose reduction strategy: toxicity is managed by infusion-rate reduction, interruption, withholding, or discontinuation
First-dose 800 mg/m2 then 600 mg/m2 q3w or 400 mg/m2 q2w; never IV push or bolus
Emetogenic: scheduled NK-1 and/or 5-HT3 based premedication before every infusion plus post-infusion antiemetics or fluids
Hypersensitivity (any grade 18%, severe 2%) and IRRs can be fatal; 2-hour post-infusion observation is required
missed: Zolbetuximab is given as supervised infusions with chemotherapy, so there is no patient-managed missed dose. If an appointment is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule; do not attempt to make up doses independently.
overdose: No specific antidote for zolbetuximab overdose is described. Manage with interruption or discontinuation, supportive care for nausea/vomiting and hypersensitivity, hydration, and monitoring of CBC, electrolytes, and renal function. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
